role: The string tag, type id 8: entity names, item ids, text pages, the keys of every mod-ish string field in saved data.
scope_reason: Part of the NBT layer behind snapshots and digests.

members.name: data
members.note: Canonical text str:<text>, a quoted span with no escapes.

members.name: NBTTagString
members.note: The empty-string constructor; canonical text str:.

members.name: NBTTagString
members.note: Java throws on a null argument; the native builder takes a non-null pointer.

members.name: write
members.note: writeUTF: a two-byte length then modified-UTF-8 bytes; nbtbin reproduces the encoding for the digest.

members.name: func_152446_a
members.note: The region reader reads the name through the same writeUTF encoding; 16 bytes per char go to the size tracker.

members.name: toString
members.note: Java's text form: built only by ItemStack.func_151000_E (the item hover in a chat line), CommandGive (chat commands are not agent input) and logging. func_151000_E runs at StatList's init on tagless stacks (id, Count, Damage: a short and a byte) and in a death message only for an item with hasDisplayName (EntityDamageSource, EntityDamageSourceIndirect, CombatTracker), and only the anvil names an item (world.conf anvil = off)

members.name: copy
members.note: The canonical text carries a string with no quote or backslash; such a string is refused rather than dropped (crafting.c copy_tag's header comment).

members.name: hashCode
members.note: Only feeds the tagMap HashMap; nbtjson.c's intern computes Java's String.hashCode once per interned key, and nbtbin.c's write_compound uses it for the bucket-order emulation, so the hash itself is reproduced where it matters.

notes: Java's hashCode is String.hashCode on the data; nbtbin.c computes the same hash for the HashMap bucket emulation, which is why the citation points at the writer rather than a hash function.
